newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Nov consumer prices rise 2.0 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Nov consumer prices rise 2.0 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted November consumer price index rose 0.4 percent in the month and 2.0 percent in the year to 136.8, Statistics Canada said Wednesday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg Nov Oct
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.4 0.0
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.4 +1.3

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally adjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month and the undadjusted CPI to rise 0.2 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 1.7 percent rise in the all-items and 1.4 percent rise in the core CPI.

Statistics Canada said the rise in the unadjusted annual index was due to an increase in auto insurance premiums in Ontario. The rise in vehicle insurance premiums added close to 0.3 percent to the monthly and annual CPI increase.

The agency said half of the 2.0 percent annual increase was due to higher transportation charges, especially for gasoline, new vehicles and vehicle insurance. Higher prices for food, university tuition, telephone services, rental accomodation and fuel oil also contributed to the gains.
Higher prices for new vehicles, auto insurance premiums in Ontario and food were the main factors behind the month-on-month CPI increase, Statistics Canada said.
